questions.question: What is the difference between a **CodeSystem** and a **ValueSet**?
options: A CodeSystem defines codes and their meanings; a ValueSet selects codes from one or more code systems for a particular use
A ValueSet defines codes; a CodeSystem selects codes from value sets for a particular use
They are the same thing: ValueSet is the newer name for CodeSystem
A CodeSystem is used in `code` elements and a ValueSet in `CodeableConcept` elements
questions.explanation: A **CodeSystem** says which codes exist and what they mean. A **ValueSet** picks the codes allowed for a purpose, and elements are bound to value sets, never directly to code systems.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit from the Condition Category value set page. What value goes in `Coding.system` for a Condition category code?
options: `http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/condition-category`
`http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/condition-category`
`ConditionCategoryCodes`
questions.explanation: The page shows two URLs. The **defining URL** (`…/ValueSet/condition-category`) identifies the value set and is what bindings point to. The codes come from the **code system** `…/CodeSystem/condition-category`, and that is what goes in `Coding.system`. The name and the OID are not system URIs.

exhibit.title: Condition Category Codes value set (FHIR R4)

questions.question: Which JSON is a valid `CodeableConcept`?
options: `{ "coding": [ { "system": "http://loinc.org", "code": "29463-7" } ], "text": "Weight" }`
`{ "coding": { "system": "http://loinc.org", "code": "29463-7" }, "text": "Weight" }`
`{ "system": "http://loinc.org", "code": "29463-7", "text": "Weight" }`
`{ "coding": [], "text": "Weight" }`
questions.explanation: `CodeableConcept.coding` is `0..*`, so it is always a JSON **array**, even with one Coding. `system` and `code` belong inside a Coding, not directly on the CodeableConcept. Empty arrays are never allowed in FHIR JSON; leave `coding` out instead.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. What is wrong with this XML?
options: Primitive values must be in a `value` attribute, e.g. `<code value="active"/>`, not between tags
`<coding>` must come after `<text>`
The `system` must be a ValueSet URL
Nothing: the XML is valid
questions.explanation: In FHIR XML, primitive values always go in the **`value` attribute**: `<system value="…"/>`, `<code value="active"/>`. Text between the tags is invalid. Inside a CodeableConcept, `<coding>` elements come **before** `<text>`, and `system` is always a code system URL.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit from the Condition structure table. Which element may carry a code that is **not** in its value set when nothing in the value set fits?
options: `category`
`clinicalStatus`
`verificationStatus`
None of them: every binding shown is required
questions.explanation: `category` has an **Extensible** binding: use a code from ConditionCategoryCodes if one applies, otherwise another code or text. `clinicalStatus` and `verificationStatus` are **Required**: only codes from their value sets are valid.

questions.question: Refer to the Terminology Bindings table for Condition. How many of the listed elements have only an **example** binding, so any suitable codes may be used?
questions.explanation: `code`, `bodySite`, `stage.summary`, `stage.type` and `evidence.code` are **Example**: five elements. `clinicalStatus` and `verificationStatus` are Required, `category` Extensible, and `severity` Preferred. Example bindings never make an instance invalid.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. Which codes are in the expansion of this value set?
options: Every LOINC code
No codes: a value set needs a filter to have members
questions.explanation: An `include` with a `concept` list selects **only the listed codes** (an extensional definition). Without the `concept` list it would include every code in LOINC. A filter is just another way to select codes, not a requirement.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit. Which statement about this value set is true?
options: It contains Diabetes mellitus (73211009) and all its descendants, except Gestational diabetes mellitus (11687002)
It contains only the two codes 73211009 and 11687002
It contains every SNOMED CT code except 73211009
It is invalid: `include` and `exclude` cannot be used together
questions.explanation: The `is-a` filter makes an **intensional** definition: the concept 73211009 plus all its descendants. The `exclude` then removes 11687002. A server works out the actual list with `$expand`.

questions.question: `Condition.verificationStatus` is a CodeableConcept with a **required** binding. A system sends `"verificationStatus": { "text": "Confirmed by the specialist" }`. Is this valid?
options: No: with a required binding at least one Coding from the value set must be present; text alone is not a substitute
Yes: `text` is always allowed instead of a Coding
Yes: required bindings only apply to `code` elements
No: CodeableConcept elements may never contain `text`
questions.explanation: For a CodeableConcept with a **required** binding, "at least one Coding element SHALL be present" and one of them SHALL be from the value set. Text is recommended alongside, but is not an acceptable substitute for the code.

questions.question: `Condition.category` (CodeableConcept) has an **extensible** binding. A research system needs a category that no code in the value set covers. What may it send?
options: Another code that fits (from any code system), or text only
Nothing: the element must be left empty
The closest code from the value set, even though it doesn’t apply
A Coding whose `system` is the ValueSet URL
questions.explanation: With an **extensible** binding, a code from the value set must be used **if any applies**. When none does (based on human review), an alternate concept may be used: another system/code pair, or, for a CodeableConcept, text alone. Never send a code that doesn’t actually apply.

questions.question: An element has an **extensible** binding. The value set contains a code that covers your concept but is more general; you also have a more specific SNOMED CT code. What does the spec require?
options: Send the value set code; the more specific code may be added as an extra Coding, but not used instead of it
Send only the more specific SNOMED CT code
Send only text, because neither code is exact
Send whichever code the user picked
questions.explanation: The spec says that if an applicable but more general concept exists in the extensibly bound value set, "the code that is used in the instance SHALL be taken from the value set". A more specific code "may also be included … as an additional Coding … but it cannot be used instead of the code from the value set".

questions.question: A CodeableConcept contains two Codings: a SNOMED CT code and an ICD-10 code. What does this mean?
options: Both codes represent the same concept in different code systems
The patient has two different conditions
The first code is the diagnosis and the second the reason
The second Coding replaces the first
questions.explanation: All Codings in one CodeableConcept represent the **same concept**, typically as translations into different code systems. Their order carries no meaning. Two different concepts need two separate CodeableConcepts or resources.

questions.question: What does `Coding.userSelected: true` indicate?
options: The user picked this exact Coding (e.g. from a pick list), as opposed to codes added by translation
The code is the preferred code in the value set
The user typed the code by hand into `display`
The Coding must be shown first in user interfaces
questions.explanation: `userSelected` marks the Coding that was chosen directly by the user. Other Codings in the CodeableConcept may have been added by mapping or translation. Order of codings has no meaning, so this flag is how you tell which one was chosen.

questions.question: Which request asks a terminology server for the codes in the Condition Category value set?
options: `GET [base]/ValueSet/$expand?url=http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/condition-category`
`GET [base]/CodeSystem/$expand?url=http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/condition-category`
`GET [base]/ValueSet/$lookup?url=http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/condition-category`
`GET [base]/ValueSet?expand=http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/condition-category`
questions.explanation: `$expand` is an operation on **ValueSet**, called with the `$` prefix; `url` identifies the value set. `$lookup` is a CodeSystem operation for one code, and `expand` is not a search parameter.

questions.question: Refer to the exhibit, a response to `$validate-code`. What does it tell the client?
options: The code is not valid in the value set; `message` explains why
The code is valid, and `message` is the code’s display
The server failed and the request should be retried
The value set could not be found
questions.explanation: `$validate-code` returns a **Parameters** resource with `result` (required) and optionally `message` and `display`. `result: false` means the code is not valid in the value set. Here the code’s case is wrong: codes are case-sensitive.

exhibit.title: $validate-code response

questions.question: Which operation returns the display, definition and properties of a single code, e.g. LOINC `29463-7`?
options: `$lookup` on CodeSystem
`$expand` on ValueSet
`$subsumes` on CodeSystem
`$translate` on ConceptMap
questions.explanation: `GET [base]/CodeSystem/$lookup?system=http://loinc.org&code=29463-7` returns details about one code. `$expand` lists a value set’s codes, `$subsumes` tests whether one code is a parent of another, and `$translate` maps a code to another code system.

questions.question: Which URL identifies the implicit value set that contains **all** LOINC codes?
options: `http://loinc.org/vs`
`http://loinc.org`
`http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/loinc`
questions.explanation: LOINC defines implicit value sets: `http://loinc.org/vs` contains every LOINC code. `http://loinc.org` is the **code system** URI used in `Coding.system`, and the OID is LOINC’s OID, not a FHIR value set URL.

questions.question: A profile needs a value set of SNOMED CT concept 73211009 (Diabetes mellitus) and all its descendants, without writing a ValueSet resource. Which URL can it use?
options: `http://snomed.info/sct?fhir_vs=isa/73211009`
`http://snomed.info/sct/73211009`
`http://snomed.info/sct?code=73211009&descendants=true`
`http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/73211009`
questions.explanation: SNOMED CT implicit value sets use the base URL plus a `fhir_vs` query: `?fhir_vs=isa/[sctid]` means the concept and all its descendants, `?fhir_vs=refset/[sctid]` the members of a reference set, and `?fhir_vs` on its own all concepts.

questions.question: A CodeSystem resource for SNOMED CT has `"content": "not-present"`. What does this mean?
options: The resource describes the code system, but its codes are not included in the resource
The code system has no codes
The code system has been retired
Only some example codes are included
questions.explanation: `CodeSystem.content` says how much of the code system the resource carries: `not-present`, `example`, `fragment`, `complete` or `supplement`. Large external terminologies are usually `not-present`; their codes are available from a terminology server.

questions.question: An Observation records a dose of 5 mg. Which `valueQuantity` uses a coded unit correctly?
options: `{ "value": 5, "unit": "mg", "system": "http://unitsofmeasure.org", "code": "mg" }`
`{ "value": 5, "unit": "mg", "system": "http://unitsofmeasure.org", "code": "milligram" }`
`{ "value": "5", "unit": "mg", "system": "http://unitsofmeasure.org", "code": "mg" }`
`{ "value": 5, "unit": "mg", "system": "http://loinc.org", "code": "mg" }`
questions.explanation: A Quantity’s unit is a coded value too: `system` = UCUM (`http://unitsofmeasure.org`) and `code` = the UCUM code `mg` (UCUM codes are case-sensitive). `unit` is just for display. `value` is a decimal, so it has **no quotes**, and LOINC does not define units.
